title: Defend Your Pieces
subtitle: A piece under attack: defend it, move it, or block.
goals: React correctly when a piece is attacked
Escape attacks WITH a threat of your own

steps.say: Your pieces will get attacked constantly — that's chess. Each time, you have options: move it, defend it, block the attack, capture the attacker, or counter-attack something bigger. The skill is choosing the RIGHT one.

steps.prompt: The f5 pawn attacks your knight — and almost every escape square is covered. Find the ONE safe square!
hints: Check each knight jump: the rook watches the d-file, the bishop covers c5, and Black's pawns cover g3, g5 and f6.
Only one landing square has no black piece eyeing it — look toward your own side.

line.say: The only safe square! Every other jump landed on a square Black controls. Checking ALL the escape squares is the habit.

rejections.say: Rxd6 — the rook owns that file. Check who's watching a square before you land there.
hxg5! The little h6 pawn was covering g5 all along.
Bxc5 — the b6 bishop had that diagonal covered.
You defended the knight with a pawn — but it doesn't help: fxe4, dxe4 and Black traded a 1-point pawn for your 3-point knight. When a PAWN attacks a piece, defending is useless — you must move it.

steps.wrongSay: That square is covered, or leaves the knight to be captured. Scan every escape square for black attackers.
steps.successSay: One safe square out of eight — and you found it. That's real board vision.

steps.prompt: The knight on g6 attacks your e5 pawn. Pawns can't run far — defend it!
hints: A pawn is best defended by another pawn — cheap labor guarding cheap labor.
Two of your pawns can step up to protect e5.

line.say: Solid! Now if Nxe5, dxe5 recaptures — the knight won't trade itself for a defended pawn.
Good! The f-pawn guards its neighbor. Nxe5 would now just lose the knight for a pawn.

rejections.say: fxe6! You pushed the pawn straight into the f7 pawn's capture zone. Running forward isn't always running to safety.

steps.wrongSay: The e5 pawn needs a bodyguard — which pawns can step up beside it?
steps.successSay: Pawns defending pawns costs you nothing — the ideal defense.

steps.prompt: The knight attacks your queen! Retreat is required — but find a retreat WITH check.
hints: The queen must move — but a move that also checks the king costs Black a whole turn.
Two squares give check along the diagonal to g8. Both are out of the knight's reach.

line.say: Saved with tempo! The queen escapes AND checks — Black must answer the check instead of continuing their plan.
Escape plus check — Black's attack gained nothing, because they now owe you a move.

rejections.say: Rxd8! That check landed on a square the b8 rook defends. A check is only free if the square is safe.

steps.wrongSay: Safe isn't enough — the best escape squares come with a check attached.
steps.successSay: Escaping with tempo — you turned a defensive moment into an attacking one.

steps.prompt: The b5 pawn attacks your bishop. Don't just survive — find the escape square that fights back!
hints: List the bishop's safe squares, then ask which one creates a threat of its own.
One diagonal square aims straight at the undefended rook in the corner.

line.say: The fighting retreat! The bishop is safe AND attacks the a8 rook — now BLACK is the one scrambling to react.

rejections.say: axb5 — the a6 pawn was guarding its partner. Count defenders even when you're the one being chased.
Safe... and completely passive. One square was safe AND created a threat — attack while you defend!
Safe, but it asks nothing of Black. The best retreat squares make threats of their own.

steps.wrongSay: Retreat, yes — but pick the square that turns defense into attack.
steps.successSay: Every forced move is a chance to improve your position. Even retreats can bite.
